subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: Should OpenClaw treat LiteLLM Vertex beta generic 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT as a provider-owned recoverable session/request-shape failure, and if so what recovery action should be allowed by default?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but generic INVALID_ARGUMENT can mean context pressure, transcript shape, media/schema rejection, auth/routing mistakes, or provider bugs; choosing compaction, fallback, non-beta routing, session cleanup, or only actionable messaging is product behavior, not a mechanical classifier tweak.

options.title: Prove and add narrow provider recovery
options.body: Run a live LiteLLM Vertex beta repro, then add a LiteLLM/provider-owned classifier and recovery path only for the proven structured error shape.

options.title: Fold into broader provider-rejection policy
options.body: Keep this evidence linked while maintainers define one generic provider-rejection recovery policy across Vertex, Anthropic, image blocks, and stalled sessions.

options.title: Keep manual reset guidance only
options.body: Leave generic INVALID_ARGUMENT unclassified and improve operator-facing diagnostics without automatic recovery, accepting that long sessions may still require /new or reset.

recommendation.title: Prove and add narrow provider recovery
recommendation.body: Run a live LiteLLM Vertex beta repro, then add a LiteLLM/provider-owned classifier and recovery path only for the proven structured error shape.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged both the LiteLLM provider surface and adjacent provider-error normalization work, and already flagged the normalization layer as incomplete in review.
